data.text:
Ito ang mensahe ni Bicol Saro Rep. Terry Ridon, chairman ng House Committee on Public Accounts, sa mga bumabatikos sa gagawing pagdinig ng kanyang komite tungkol sa pangangailangang gawin ang P389-million Dolomite Beach project noong 2022.

"Kabahan na kayo kung 'yan 'yung dahilan bakit ho kayo merong mga ongoing troll attacks laban sa investigation pong ito," sinabi ni Ridon sa 'Facts First' podcast ng veteran broadcast-journalist na si Christian Esguerra kamakailan.

Sa Nobyembre 17 itinakda ang hearing kung saan aalamin ng Kamara kung naaayon ba ang dolomite beach sa Manila Bay Sustainable Development Master Plan at sa writ of continuing mandamus ng Korte Suprema sa rehabilitasyon ng Manila Bay.

Aalamin din ng komite ni Ridon kung may kinalaman ang dolomite beach sa paglala ng baha sa paligid ng Manila Bay, kabilang ang Ermita at Malate areas.

Imbitado ng Kamara sa nasabing pagdinig ang mga kinatawan mula sa Department of Environment and Natural Resources (DENR), Department of Economy, Planning and Development, Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH), Metropolitan Manila Development Authority (MMDA), at Manila City government.

DWM SPECIAL UPDATE ABOUT MJO & ROSSBY RETURN, DATED: 4TH NOV 2025  

TOPIC: WET NOVEMBER AHEAD WITH PLANETARY WAVE ARRIVAL!  

1. The evolving strong negative Indian Ocean Dipole conditions and La Nina background are creating favourable conditions for planetary wave arrivals.  

2. Sea surface temperatures greater than 29–30°C remain confined to the eastern Indian Ocean, Maritime Continent, and western Pacific Ocean.  

3. According to Wheeler-Hendon reanalysis (1979–2023), the MJO is likely to spend more time in Phases 3, 4, and 5 during negative IOD and La Nina years.  

4. Historical patterns suggest the MJO has repeatedly re-initiated in Phases 3 and 4 during NIOD background. Cai et al. (2019) stated that negative IOD increases MJO amplitude in the eastern Indian Ocean by 40% compared to neutral and positive IOD years.  

5. A strong Walker circulation and favourable SSTs are slowing the MJO's progression and promoting re-initiation between November and January over the eastern Indian Ocean and Maritime Continent.  

6. Currently, the MJO has weakened significantly upon attempting to enter Phase 6 and has been pushed back to Phase 5.  

7. The Phase 5 MJO resulted in Typhoon Kalmaegi over the western Pacific. Following this, another super-strong typhoon is expected to form around 8th November and impact northern Philippines and Taiwan during 10–12th November 2025.  

8. An equatorial Rossby wave is expected to reach the eastern Indian Ocean after mid-November, with MJO re-initiation likely around 20th November. As a result, the second half of November is forecast to see excess rainfall activity.  

9. The anticipated breakdown of the negative IOD is expected to further enhance rainfall and support active cyclogenesis over the North Indian Ocean during Second half of November and December.  

10. Overall, a vigorous Northeast monsoon is on the cards, with the second half of the season appearing particularly active and wet.
